issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
**What I need:** for the review of the Iris LR vs k-NN study, the analysis outputs need to include the evidence that lets the claims be checked, not only summaries:

1. Per-fold accuracies of both methods for all 50 outer folds (10 reps x stratified 5-fold, same splits for both), with rep/fold/seed columns and the k chosen by inner CV in each fold — from **both** the Ibex run and the local run, as separate files.
2. Ibex evidence: SLURM job id, the job's own stdout/log showing the node name (`$SLURMD_NODENAME` or `hostname` printed by the job; `sacct -j <id> -o JobID,NodeList,State,Elapsed` is a good complement), and Python/numpy/scikit-learn versions on Ibex and locally.
3. The equality check as code output: exact comparison (or hash) of the full per-fold files of the two runs, not of rounded summaries.
4. Data provenance: how dataset 61 was fetched from OpenML (URL/API, dataset version) and a checksum of the file used.
5. The interval method named in the outputs. Note for planning: repeated-CV folds share training data, so a plain t-interval over 50 folds treated as independent is anti-conservative; I will expect either the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t (test/train = 1/4) or an interval over the 10 repetition means, or a stated justification for another choice. Reporting the naive one alongside is fine.

**What it is for:** verifying the claims the report will make (mean accuracy ± 95% interval per method, paired difference ± 95% interval, Ibex node name, identical-or-not), and re-running the code myself to confirm the numbers reproduce.

**What I know:** the full review standard is pushed in this repository at `review/STANDARD.md` (commit 09ae1b747892826ff6014fbd30eafa138f3ab330), items R1–R5 concern your part.

**What waits on it:** my verdict on the analysis and on every number in the report. Close this when the outputs above are pushed (pointing to the files), or tell me which item you will not supply and why.
issue.title: Verification evidence for review: per-fold outputs of both runs, Ibex node log, equality check, interval method

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Pushed at `c7888393c553c99f207850d46bdfabdb23c47fae`. Your items, in order:

1. Per-fold results from both runs, as separate files: `report/results/local/folds.csv` and `report/results/ibex/folds.csv`, with columns `repeat`, `fold`, `outer_seed`, `inner_seed` and `k_selected`. Both methods use the same splits: `test_index_sha1` is per split, and `predictions.csv` lists every test index.
2. Ibex: job 53909302. The job's own log is `report/results/ibex/rw-c143f1f93f2f-cv-53909302.out`, which prints `SLURMD_NODENAME=cn511-08`, the CPU and sacct. Post-completion sacct (COMPLETED, cn511-08, batch) is in `report/results/ibex/sacct_after.txt`. Versions on each side are in `report/results/{local,ibex}/env.json`.
3. Equality as code output: `report/code/compare_runs.py` → `report/results/reproducibility.json`. It compares folds, predictions and every summary float element-wise and records sha256 hashes of all three files: `identical` = true and every max abs difference is 0.
4. Data provenance: `report/code/fetch_data.py` → `report/results/provenance.json` (API URL, file URL, version 1, md5 = OpenML's, sha256). Both runs assert the md5, and `same_data_file` = true.
5. Interval method: the primary is the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t with test/train = 30/120 (`protocol.interval_primary` in `summary.json`). Naive and repetition-mean intervals are reported alongside.

To re-run, from `report/`: `pip install -r code/requirements.txt` (Python 3.11.2), then `python code/cv_compare.py /tmp/x` (about 25 s). Compare the result with `results/local`.

One disclosure: the primary k grid is the plan's {1,3,…,31}. My first run, made before I had read the plan, used {1,…,30}. It is kept as robustness variant `k_grid_all_1_30` in `report/results/robustness.json`, and the conclusion is the same.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Pushed at `c7888393c553c99f207850d46bdfabdb23c47fae` under the assigned paths `report/code/` and `report/results/`. Cite `report/results/local/summary.json` (S) and `report/results/reproducibility.json` (R). `report/results/README.md` explains every file and ends with a findings summary.

1–2. S → `logistic_regression`, `knn`, `difference_lr_minus_knn`: `mean`, and `corrected.lo/hi` (primary). The method is the corrected resampled t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004): mean ± t(0.975,49)·s·√(1/50+30/120). It is used because folds of repeated CV share training data, which makes a plain t interval too narrow; the `naive` and `repeat` intervals are reported only for comparison. The difference interval contains 0 (p = 0.54, `corrected.p_two_sided_vs_0`), so the claim the plan allows is "no difference resolved", not "equivalent". Wins, losses and ties: `folds_lr_better`, `folds_knn_better`, `folds_tied`.
3. S → `protocol` (`k_grid`, `inner`, tie rule), `k_selected_counts`, `k_selected_median`, `k_selected_at_grid_edge`.
4. S → `protocol.lr`, `protocol.preprocessing`, `protocol.outer_seed`. `lr_multinomial_verified` = true and `convergence_warnings` = 0.
5. R → `ibex_job_id`, `ibex_node`, `ibex_partition`, `identical` (element-wise on folds, all 1500 per-sample predictions and every summary float), and `env.local` / `env.ibex` (versions and CPUs). The job's own log is `report/results/ibex/rw-c143f1f93f2f-cv-53909302.out`, and the post-completion sacct output is `report/results/ibex/sacct_after.txt`.
6. `report/results/provenance.json`: URL, version 1, md5 equal to OpenML's, sha256. n = 150, 4 features and 3×50 classes are asserted in `code/cv_compare.py`.

Secondary results, if space allows a sentence: `report/results/robustness.json`. Under every variant (other k grids, no standardisation, LR with tuned C, three other outer seeds) the corrected interval for the difference contains 0.

To generate macros, read these JSON keys rather than the README text, which rounds.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Logistic regression against k-nearest neighbours on the Iris data: a small comparison written up as a short paper.

Data. Use the Iris dataset from OpenML (dataset id 61), downloaded from OpenML itself.

Study. Compare multinomial logistic regression with k-nearest neighbours (choose k by inner cross-validation) by 10 repetitions of stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Report each method's mean accuracy with a 95% interval and the paired difference with its 95% interval. Run the full cross-validation once as a CPU job on the Ibex cluster and once locally, and report the node name of the Ibex job and whether the two runs give identical numbers.

Paper. `report/report.pdf`, at most two pages in the NeurIPS 2026 submission template, compiled from LaTeX, with one figure, one table and the code that produced every number. Deliver the LaTeX source and the code next to the PDF.

issue.title: Review findings on the report draft: page limit, placeholders, numbers code, captions, conclusion wording

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
Findings at paper-repo `8387919cc4bbd311c450819132de4c5ce2e0a8b8` (each must hold in the final `report/report.pdf`):

1. **Page limit.** `latexmk -pdf report.tex` (TeX Live 2026) on the assembled delivery gives **3 pages**; the references fall on page 3, and that is with short `\TBD` placeholders. Venue V2 (venue-repo `venue/REQUIREMENTS.md`) requires the whole PDF ≤ 2 pages, references included, without margin/font/`\vspace` hacks. Shorten text, consider a lower figure height or placing figure and table side by side, trim references to those cited for claims.
2. **Placeholders.** Every number (`\LRmean` … `\Ties`) and the Discussion conclusion are still `\TBD`. All values now exist in experiment-repo's `report/results/` (see the issue body).
3. **Code for the paper's numbers.** `report/README.md` says `numbers.tex` is generated by `build_numbers.py`, which is not in the delivery. The objective requires the code that produced every number next to the PDF: deliver the generator (e.g. under `report/`) and make `numbers.tex` its output, reading `report/results/*` files only.
4. **Captions name the interval.** The table and figure captions in `report.tex` say "95% intervals" without the method. Name it (corrected resampled t, Nadeau & Bengio 2003) in both, as the brief §5.2 and figtab's caption files (`report/tables/results_table_caption.txt`, `report/figures/accuracy_fig_caption.txt`) do; state that bounds are not clipped at 100%.
5. **Conclusion matches the primary interval.** The primary corrected interval for LR−kNN is [−2.14, +4.00] pp and includes 0. The naive interval over 50 folds (+0.10, +1.77) and the repetition-mean interval (+0.42, +1.45) both exclude 0. If either is mentioned, label it as ignoring the dependence between folds (or, for the repetition-mean interval, as capturing only split-to-split variation on the same 150 points), never as evidence that LR is more accurate. Report the fold counts (13 LR better, 5 kNN better, 32 tied) as description, not as a test.
6. **For figtab-repo (please pass on; it is not my neighbour):** `report/figures/__pycache__/stats.cpython-311.pyc` is a compiled bytecode file inside the delivered path. Remove it and ignore `__pycache__/`.

I will judge the next revision by recompiling the PDF from the delivered source, checking the page count, the template options, one figure and one table, and every printed number against `report/results/`.

comments.author: paper-repo
comments.body:
Revision pushed: paper-repo `bd7dea1e17d076bc27607e3e829b994ff13851c1`. `report/report.pdf` is now committed. It was compiled from the assembled delivery: experiment-repo 2bcd5889596e, figtab-repo 4e157f2b1d3c, venue-repo 169514aed063. Item by item:

1. **Page limit.** The whole PDF is **2 pages**, references included (`pdfinfo`), with no overfull boxes or undefined references in `report.log`. I shortened the text and changed no margins, fonts, `\vspace` or template options; the template is still the default `\usepackage{neurips_2026}` submission mode. I re-assembled the delivery at the pushed revision with `ht-role delivery` and the build still gives 2 pages.
2. **Placeholders.** None are left. Every number in the text is a macro in `report/numbers.tex`, and the Discussion states the conclusion: LR and tuned kNN cannot be told apart, difference −2.1 to +4.0 pp.
3. **Code for the paper's numbers.** `report/make_numbers.py` (in this repo) writes `numbers.tex`, reading only `report/results/{local/summary.json, reproducibility.json, provenance.json, robustness.json}`. It asserts multinomial LR, an Ibex node that matches the job log, element-wise identity, equal software versions on both machines and the OpenML MD5. Running it in the assembled delivery reproduces the committed `numbers.tex` byte for byte. `report/README.md` maps each macro to its file and key; the stale `build_numbers.py` reference was already gone at 82825c9.
4. **Captions.** Both captions now say "95% corrected resampled *t* interval (Nadeau and Bengio, 2003), not clipped at 100%". The figure caption also describes the jittered points, the mean marker and the dashed zero line, all of which match figtab's figure.
5. **Conclusion wording.** The primary corrected interval [−2.1, +4.0] pp (p = 0.54) is reported as not resolving a difference. The naive 50-fold interval (+0.1 to +1.8) appears only once, labelled as ignoring the dependence between folds, which "would wrongly suggest an advantage for LR". The repetition-mean interval is not mentioned. The 13/5/32 fold counts appear only as description. The sensitivity sentence now reads "In all 8 sensitivity variants … the interval also contains zero", from `robustness.json`: 8 variants besides `main`.
6. **`__pycache__` in figures.** Passed on to figtab-repo as figtab-repo#5, together with a hyphen-vs-minus fix in the table's CI (`[-2.14` → `$-$2.14`). Neither changes the layout or any value.

issue.author: idea-review-repo
issue.body:
Feasibility finds the study feasible (tiny compute); full probes and bounds are in world/idea-review-repo `feasibility.md`. What the plan/assignment should carry so it meets the objective:

1. **Identical-numbers check.** The Ibex login python has scikit-learn 1.5.0 / numpy 2.1.2; the local sandbox venv has no sklearn (unpinned pip gives 1.9.1). The experiment owner must pin the same versions locally, set single-thread BLAS, fixed per-repetition seeds, and define "identical" up front (bit-exact fold-level CSV, else report max abs diff honestly). Record node name via `hostname`/`$SLURMD_NODENAME` inside the job.
2. **Data.** Fetch OpenML id 61 from OpenML (reachable from sandbox and Ibex login node; compute-node network untested, local-compute has no network). Pre-fetch, record SHA-256, use the same file in both runs.
3. **Intervals.** 50 overlapping CV folds are not independent; pick and state one interval method (e.g. Nadeau-Bengio corrected t, or t-interval over the 10 repeat means) for both-method means and the paired difference; name it in the table caption.
4. **Protocol.** Fix k-grid, inner-CV seeds and tie-break rule in advance; scaling inside the pipeline; fix LR's C (or tune both methods).
5. **Page limit.** Whole PDF <= 2 pages in the NeurIPS 2026 template (zip at media.neurips.cc/Conferences/NeurIPS2026/Formatting_Instructions_For_NeurIPS_2026.zip: neurips_2026.tex/.sty, checklist.tex). Assume checklist and references count; keep text short. Assign this to venue/paper.
6. **Scheduling.** The Ibex `batch` queue is ~full: submit the Ibex job as soon as the code is fixed (`ht-resource track ibex`), run local in parallel, and do not let paper/figtab wait on anything else. Every number in the report must come from committed scripts reading the result files.

comments.body:

Identity: §2 "Seeds and environment" (pin local to the Ibex scikit-learn 1.5.0 / numpy 2.1.2, or the same lock on both; single-thread BLAS) and §3, which fixes the criterion before comparing: element-wise equal fold-level results (accuracies, chosen k, per-sample predictions) and float-equal summaries, otherwise max abs difference per quantity and the splits that differ; node name, job id and hostname recorded from inside the job.

comments.body:
Answers (pushed in venue-repo 087d9ac1b31ae872abe5af2360818a9d295a2055; full text in venue/REQUIREMENTS.md, template files unmodified in venue/):
1. Style file: venue/neurips_2026.sty (official, from media.neurips.cc, checksums in venue/SHA256SUMS). Copy it to report/neurips_2026.sty (report/ is your path) so the source rebuilds. Preamble: plain `\usepackage{neurips_2026}` (main track, anonymous, line numbers). No `final` (accepted papers only), no `preprint`. Keep the author block anonymous.
2. Limit: official NeurIPS limit is 9 content pages and excludes ack/references/checklist/appendix, but the objective's 'at most two pages' is stricter and governs: total report.pdf <= 2 pages, references included (strict reading), keep the reference list tiny. The NeurIPS checklist (venue/checklist.tex) cannot fit and is omitted; this conflict is recorded in REQUIREMENTS.md.
3. Other rules: do not alter margins/fonts or load fullpage; 10pt, abstract one paragraph; figure caption BELOW figure, table caption ABOVE table, captions lower case except first word/proper nouns; booktabs, no vertical rules; legible in B/W; exactly one figure and one table. Deliver report.tex + any .bib/.sty/figure files + code next to the PDF; check with pdfinfo (Pages <= 2). Code path will come from assignment.json; I'll add it to venue-artifacts.json then.
